chapter: First bands, Ennis, Thornhill and the Army
title: Skinny Ennis takes over Gil's band
summary: Gil describes how MCA put Ennis in front of his band, how its library changed to Ennis's sound and why he left.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: And it probably surprised you too, huh? (LAUGHTER). What was it like working for Skinny (Ennis?)? He has something of a .......
It was fairly miserable.
Yes, that's what I was going to say, he has something of a .......

When we first started I had, it was my band and my library you know. So he took the band over and the first couple of jobs we played he would stand out front and listen to it you know. And he liked it very much and when the number would be over he would applaud and everything, forgetting that he was the leader of the thing, you know. (LAUGHTER).
And he'd just taken over, huh?
And when they decided that what he had to do was do what he had done to be a

hit, he had been with a band, Hal Kemp, a very popular band. Skinny had a little whispering kind of a instrumental pattern, continental sound you know. Although he sang, he didn't sing in a foreign language or anything, he had that kind of sound and he was becoming very popular in England and all over.
And so, the manager and I decided he had to do that kind of music. So gradually the library got changed to his kind of music and then I left.
I remember, I'm sure I remember Skinny (Ennis's) broadcasting years ago from the deep South somewhere. Right, no?
I don't think so. He was always in California.
Always in California?
He was a Cracker. He came from Salisbury, North Carolina?
Yes, Carolina?
From Salisbury, and, yeah, a total Southern Cracker but at the same time all his work was in Hollywood. He worked for Bob Hope, he was on that show for years.
Yes.
Oh that's right, he got drafted too, that's right. Les Brown got the job and then .........
I don't know, it just seems to me that I remember him from the years back before he got on big time, he really hit the big time.
Well he was with Hal Kemp's band and they may have played that territory. I'm sure they did, they were all from there..........
What was the advantage of turning your band over to him?
It was work for everybody. We had no work. (We had to do something?), so MCA made me this offer.......
Oh, because they, they thought that he had a bigger name at that point or would be a bigger drawing card or what?

Yes, they couldn't get me any work at all. So, and they could get him work so we took the job. And the same band from Stockton working for a while and then we gradually drifted apart, you know. He hired other people and some
of us left you know, and so finally there was no one left of the original band.
